Build the raster graph from covariates and sampling sites

Source: R/radish_graph.R
conductance_surface.Rd

Reads spatial covariates and focal-point coordinates and builds a weighted graph suitable for computing conductance-weighted resistance distances. This is the first step of every terradish workflow.

Usage

conductance_surface(
  covariates,
  coords,
  directions = 8,
  saveStack = TRUE,
  crop_buffer = NULL
)

Arguments

covariates

A SpatRaster (or PackedSpatRaster) whose layers contain the spatial covariates to be used in the conductance model. Layer names must match the right-hand side of the formula passed to terradish. Name the layers first, then scale continuous layers with scale_covariates before calling this function.

coords

Locations of the focal sampling sites, in the same coordinate reference system as covariates. Supported inputs: terra::SpatVector of points, a two-column numeric matrix (x in column 1, y in column 2), or a data frame with columns named x and y (or at least two columns, using the first two).

directions

Adjacency rule for the graph. 4 connects each cell to its four horizontal/vertical neighbors (rook adjacency); 8 additionally includes the four diagonal neighbors (queen adjacency). 8 is recommended for landscape genetics: it allows diagonal movement, produces smoother resistance surfaces, and is less sensitive to grid orientation artifacts.

saveStack

Logical. If TRUE (default), the masked SpatRaster is stored inside the returned terradish_graph object. Required for raster-based conductance visualization (plot(fit, type = "surface")) and marginal-association plots. Set to FALSE to reduce memory use when the raster is large and visualization is not needed.

crop_buffer

Optional nonnegative map-unit buffer to crop covariates around the focal coordinates before graph construction. When supplied, crop_to_focal_buffer is called internally. A scalar applies the same buffer in both x and y directions; a length-two vector gives c(x_buffer, y_buffer). Units are the raster's map units (degrees for lon/lat, meters for projected rasters). See Details.

Value

An object of class "terradish_graph" (also inheriting "radish_graph") containing:

demes

Integer indices of cells corresponding to focal sites.

x

Data frame of covariate values at non-missing cells.

adj

Edge list (upper-triangular, 0-based).

edge_pairs

Integer matrix of adjacent cell pairs.

vertex_coordinates

xy-coordinate matrix of active cells.

directions

The adjacency rule (4 or 8).

covariates

Names of the covariate columns.

laplacian, rhs, reduced_index, choleski_templates, choleski

Internal solver state: the reduced graph Laplacian template, the right-hand sides for the focal sites, the retained vertex index, and symbolic sparse Cholesky factorizations. These are reused by the fitting functions and are not meant to be modified.

stack

The masked SpatRaster (or NULL if saveStack = FALSE).

Details

Missing values: NA is propagated uniformly across all layers so every cell is either complete or entirely missing. A warning is issued if some cells are NA in only a subset of layers, because this indicates that different covariates cover different areas; model comparison across raster stacks with different NA patterns is problematic since the graph vertices differ. Always compare models using the same terradish_graph object.

Disconnected components: after masking, the graph may contain cells that are isolated from the main component. The function retains only the largest connected component and warns about the number of pruned cells. The function aborts if any focal site belongs to a disconnected component.

Cropping: when crop_buffer is supplied, cropping changes the graph domain. Always use the same terradish_graph for all models you intend to compare. Cropping removes possible movement paths and can inflate resistance. In an unpublished development check on one landscape, resistance increased by 15–23 percent with a two-cell buffer and by 1–2 percent with ten cells. These are case-specific results; refit with several buffer values before interpreting a cropped landscape.

Categorical covariates: raster layers representing categorical variables must be stored as factor-valued SpatRaster layers (see as.factor and the example below). Level names are taken from the VALUE column of the levels table when present; otherwise the first non-ID column is used. Factor levels are dummy-coded by model.matrix during model fitting, with one level as the reference.

Directions: eight-neighbor adjacency is the default and is preferred unless there is a specific reason to restrict movement to the cardinal directions. directions = 4 removes the diagonal edges, so it can overstate resistance (understate connectivity) along diagonal corridors. Each edge has conductance \(c_i + c_j\); diagonal edges receive no additional distance weighting.

Sites sharing a cell: two or more focal sites that fall in the same raster cell trigger a warning, because their resistance distance is zero. Use a finer raster, or keep one site per cell as in the example.

See also

Other graph setup: crop_to_focal_buffer(), scale_covariates()

Examples

library(terra)

data(melip)
covariates <- c(terra::unwrap(melip.altitude),
                terra::unwrap(melip.forestcover))
coords <- terra::unwrap(melip.coords)

# Name the layers first, then scale them.
names(covariates) <- c("altitude", "forestcover")
covariates <- scale_covariates(covariates)

# A few melip sites fall in the same raster cell. Keep one site per cell
# (and the matching rows and columns of the genetic matrix).
keep <- !duplicated(terra::cellFromXY(covariates, terra::crds(coords)))
coords <- coords[keep]
Fst <- melip.Fst[keep, keep]

surface <- conductance_surface(covariates, coords)  # eight neighbors
surface$directions
#> [1] 8
nrow(surface$x)       # number of graph vertices (non-missing cells)
#> [1] 22443
length(surface$demes) # number of focal sites
#> [1] 34

# For large rasters where sites occupy only part of the map, crop first.
surface_cropped <- conductance_surface(covariates, coords,
                                       crop_buffer = 0.05)
#> The crop buffer is less than half the maximum distance between focal sites. Cropping can inflate resistance; compare fits with a larger buffer.

# Categorical covariates must be factor-valued layers (see Details).
forestcover <- terra::unwrap(melip.forestcover)
forestcover_class <- cut(terra::values(forestcover)[, 1],
                         breaks = c(0, 1/6, 1/3, 1))
forestcover_cat <- terra::setValues(forestcover,
                                    as.numeric(forestcover_class))
forestcover_cat <- terra::as.factor(forestcover_cat)
RAT <- levels(forestcover_cat)[[1]]
RAT$VALUE <- levels(forestcover_class) # explicitly define level names
levels(forestcover_cat) <- RAT
names(forestcover_cat) <- "forestcover"

surface_cat <- conductance_surface(forestcover_cat, coords)
levels(surface_cat$x$forestcover)
#> NULL
